audience: The public-sector middle manager who commissions the assessment, defends its result to the minister and plans what to build first

videos.title: What makes infrastructure foundational
videos.message: Before you fund anything called "DPI", test it against four marks: it serves the whole society, many services can connect to it, it is built on open standards, and clear rules govern it.

videos.title: The five domains, as a map
videos.message: One page with five domains, a foundation of governance, policy and law carrying access, digital data, interoperability and digital identity, shows your minister what the country has and what it lacks.

videos.title: The roadmap method in nine steps: who does what
videos.message: A roadmap is produced in nine steps, and for each step you can say who acts, what goes in, what comes out, who decides and how the result is checked.

videos.title: Start at the desk: a first assessment from public sources, with AI
videos.message: An AI-assisted review of what your country has already published gives you first findings and gaps before you ask anyone a question, each tied to its source, and it is a draft to verify, not a verdict.

videos.title: Ask the people who run the systems: the five questionnaires
videos.message: Five questionnaires, one for each domain, put the same questions to the people who run the systems and ask for evidence with every answer.

videos.title: Verify before you score
videos.message: An answer becomes a finding only when it has been checked against documents, in interviews and workshops, and in a validation session with the people who gave it.

videos.title: Score each domain: five stages and one table
videos.message: Score each domain on five published stages against written criteria, so that two assessors reach the same result and the whole picture fits on one table.

videos.title: Foundational blocks and the sector's own
videos.message: Identity, payments and data exchange are foundations for every sector, while a learner register and its registration service belong to education and stand on them, and each must be funded as what it is.

videos.title: What comes first: the order of building
videos.message: Build identity and payments first, bring in data exchange and registration with the first priority services, digitalise the registers next, and show one visible result early so that support holds.

videos.title: The first proof for education: one service on four blocks
videos.message: The first proof for education is one service that registers a learner once: the sector's own registration service and learner register, using the country's identity and payment blocks through the data exchange layer.
